extracted.intended_audience: hospital coders, Medicare IPPS/LTCH providers, health information management professionals, hospital finance staff, and stakeholders submitting public comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for ICD-10 code maintenance, CC/MCC exclusion logic, surgical hierarchy ordering, new code assignment, data cleaning, and methodology for developing FY 2027 MS-DRG relative weights under the IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the CC Exclusions List
rubrics_metrics.description: Create CC Exclusions List to: (1) preclude coding of CCs for closely related conditions; (2) preclude duplicative or inconsistent coding from being treated as CCs; and (3) ensure that cases are appropriately classified between the complicated and uncomplicated DRGs in a pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains historical background (September 1, 1987 final notice) and rationale for excluding certain secondary diagnoses from counting as CCs when combined with particular principal diagnoses; the CC Exclusions List is maintained to avoid inappropriate severity assignment due to related or conflicting codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CC Exclusion List principles (five principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The excluded secondary diagnoses were established using five principles: (1) chronic and acute manifestations of the same condition should not be considered CCs for one another; (2) specific and nonspecific (NOS) diagnosis codes for the same condition should not be considered CCs for one another; (3) codes for the same condition that cannot coexist (e.g., partial/total, unilateral/bilateral, obstructed/unobstructed, benign/malignant) should not be considered CCs for one another; (4) codes for the same condition in anatomically proximal sites should not be considered CCs for one another; (5) closely related conditions should not be considered CCs for one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five principles guide inclusion/exclusion decisions for CC logic to prevent double-counting or inappropriate severity increases when codes reflect related aspects of the same clinical entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and parts of the ICD-10 MS-DRG CC Exclusion List
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICD-10 MS-DRG CC Exclusion List (Version 43.1) includes three parts: Part 1 — list of all diagnosis codes defined as a CC or MCC when reported secondary with links to principal diagnoses that would cause the CC/MCC to be considered a NonCC; Part 2 — diagnosis codes designated as an MCC only for patients discharged alive (otherwise assigned as a NonCC); Part 3 — diagnosis codes designated as a CC or MCC and included in logic for listed MS-DRGs where, when reported secondary and grouped to those MS-DRGs, the diagnosis is excluded from acting as a CC/MCC (suppression logic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how the lists are organized and what each part means for grouping logic; Part 1/2/3 distinctions determine when a secondary diagnosis counts as CC/MCC, counts only for discharged-alive cases, or is suppressed for specific MS-DRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How proposed additions/deletions to CC Exclusions Lists are presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables 6G.1/6G.2 (additions) and 6H.1/6H.2 (deletions) show proposed changes: for 6G.1 each secondary diagnosis proposed for addition is shown with an asterisk and the principal diagnoses proposed to exclude it are indented immediately following; for 6G.2 each principal diagnosis for which there is a CC exclusion is shown with an asterisk and the conditions proposed for addition are indented immediately following; for 6H.1 each secondary diagnosis proposed for deletion is shown with an asterisk followed by the principal diagnosis codes that currently exclude it; for 6H.2 each principal diagnosis is shown with an asterisk and proposed deletions are indented immediately following.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the table formatting and notation so readers can interpret which codes are being added or removed and the relationship between secondary and principal diagnoses in the exclusion logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: New/revised/invalid code tables availability and commentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables 6A–6E (new diagnosis/procedure codes, invalid codes, revised diagnosis code titles) are available on the CMS website and are not published in the Addendum to the proposed rule; code titles are adopted as part of the ICD-10 Coordination and Maintenance Committee process and 'are not subject to comment in the proposed or final rules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs readers to CMS website for full tables and clarifies that code titles themselves are not open for comment via the proposed/final rulemaking process because titles are adopted via the Committee process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach for proposing MDC and MS-DRG assignments for new codes
rubrics_metrics.description: To propose MDC and MS-DRG assignments and attributes (severity level, O.R. status) for new diagnosis and procedure codes, CMS examines the predecessor code and MS-DRG assignment most closely associated with the new code and, in the absence of claims data, considers other factors including severity of illness, treatment difficulty, complexity of service and resources utilized in diagnosis/treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that examination of predecessor code informs proposed assignments, but 'this process does not automatically result in the new diagnosis or procedure code being proposed for assignment to the same MS-DRG or to have the same designation as the predecessor code.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical hierarchy methodology (ordering surgical classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgical classes are ordered from most resource-intensive to least resource-intensive by weighting the average resources for each MS-DRG in the class by frequency (number of cases) to determine the weighted average resources for the surgical class; classes are then ranked by average weighted cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains example calculation, notes this ordering ensures cases with multiple surgical procedures are assigned to the MS-DRG associated with the most resource-intensive class, and that application of hierarchy may sometimes assign a case to a lower-weighted MS-DRG within the highest surgical class because GROUPER searches in the most resource-intensive class. Also notes potential need to adjust other MS-DRG hierarchies to preserve monotonicity of average weighted cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical hierarchy exceptions and special ordering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Two exceptions noted: (1) 'other O.R. procedures' surgical class is uniformly ordered last in each MDC regardless of average costs; (2) when differences in average costs between classes are very small, CMS generally will not reorder the hierarchy because reassigning cases could shift averages and invert ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rationale for exceptions: 'other O.R. procedures' are infrequently related to MDC diagnoses and should be used only if no more closely related class applies; small cost differences do not warrant reordering due to instability after reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and submission process for MS-DRG issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties are encouraged to submit comments (for surgical hierarchy issues and other MS-DRG related requests) by October 20, 2026 via MEARIS (https://mearis.cms.gov/public/home) so they can be considered for inclusion in the annual proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism and deadline for submitting input on proposed MS-DRG classification and hierarchy changes; elsewhere the document gives additional meeting-specific deadlines and email addresses for code-specific input.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICD-10 Coordination and Maintenance Committee roles and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee (co-chaired by NCHS and CMS) is charged with maintaining/updating ICD-10-CM/PCS, approving coding changes, developing errata/addenda/modifications, encouraging education and standardization, and making code request materials and proposed coding changes publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains committee's joint responsibility, encourages participation from health-related organizations and individuals, and notes that after public comments the Committee formulates recommendations that must be approved by CDC/NCHS and CMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation procedures, submission points, and meeting timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public may submit diagnosis code comments to CDC/NCHS (nchsICD-10-CM@cdc.gov) and procedure code comments to CMS (ICDProcedureCodeRequest@cms.hhs.gov). The Committee posts meeting materials and provides timelines for comment; specific meeting deadlines cited include deadlines for Fall 2025 and Spring 2026 meetings and comment windows tied to April 1 and October 1 implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes dates/deadlines (e.g., Fall 2025 procedure code comment deadlines Oct 10, 2025 and Nov 14, 2025; Spring 2026 ICD-10-PCS procedure code deadlines April 17, 2026) and directs readers to CDC and CMS web pages for meeting recordings/materials and instructions on requesting new codes or participating in meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: April 1 vs October 1 code update process and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 503(a) of Public Law 108-173 requires adding new diagnosis and procedure codes on April 1 and October 1 each year; April 1 additions do not require payment or DRG adjustments until the fiscal year beginning after such date. CMS implemented an April 1 update mechanism to recognize new technologies earlier; requestors indicate desired implementation date but the Committee ultimately determines which requests are presented for April 1 or October 1 consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes historical process (strong convincing case previously required for April 1 consideration) and states current practice: same consideration process for all April 1 requests, Committee makes reasonable efforts but may postpone requests if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for replaced devices offered without cost or with a credit
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS policy reduces a hospital's IPPS payment for certain MS-DRGs when the implantation of a device that subsequently failed or was recalled determined the base MS-DRG assignment and the hospital received a credit for a replaced device equal to 50 percent or more of the cost of the device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes prior clarifications and that existing MS-DRGs subject to this policy are mapped to newly formed MS-DRGs when procedures move to new DRGs; proposed additions of new MS-DRGs (e.g., 210, 211, 449) to the list are contingent on finalization of MS-DRG changes. Final list will be in final rule and issued via Change Request (CR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and software release procedures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS issues Change Requests and transmittals for GROUPER and MCE releases (example: CR 14337 Transmittal 13562 issued Dec 23, 2025 for GROUPER/MCE Version V43.1 effective April 1, 2026). New codes are announced (example: November 2025) and code files made available (example: December 2025); NCHS publishes Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting (example: January 2026); updated GROUPER software posted (example: Feb 3, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies where to obtain updated software and manuals (CMS website links) and that updates reflect the new procedure codes and MS-DRG GROUPER versions; encourages stakeholders to use posted files and CHANGE REQUESTs for operational updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: MedPAR claims inclusion/exclusion criteria for relative weight calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative weights are based on FY 2025 MedPAR claims (discharges Oct 1, 2024–Sep 30, 2025). Exclusions: Medicare Advantage managed care claims (GHO Paid=1 or IME-only claims), claims with claim type values not equal to '60' (inpatient fee-for-service), CAHs and REHs are excluded, and discharges for beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Advantage are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how the MedPAR dataset was filtered to represent fee-for-service inpatient claims only and to exclude facility types not subject to IPPS in the analysis period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost report data source and CCR usage for relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: The second data source for cost-based relative weighting is HCRIS Medicare cost report files; CMS generally uses the HCRIS dataset that is three years prior to the IPPS fiscal year (for FY 2027 proposed rule, the December 2025 update of FY 2024 HCRIS) and uses 19 cost-to-charge ratios (CCRs) in the methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides the specific HCRIS version used and posts the CCRs on the CMS website for transparency and reproducibility of the relative weight calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data cleaning and exclusions for relative weight calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims with total charges or total lengths of stay less than or equal to zero are deleted; claims whose total charge field differs by more than $30.00 from the sum of specified cost center charges are deleted; providers that do not have charges greater than zero for at least 14 of the 19 cost centers are deleted (provider must have no more than five blank cost centers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the cost centers checked (e.g., routine day, intensive care, pharmacy, implantable devices, supplies/equipment, therapy services, O.R., cardiology, lab, radiology, other services, labor and delivery, inhalation therapy, emergency room, blood/products, anesthesia, cardiac cath, CT, MRI). These cleaning steps are used prior to computing average costs and eliminating statistical outliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transplant case selection and cost adjustments in weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Transplant cases used to establish relative weights for certain transplant MS-DRGs are limited to Medicare-approved transplant centers that have cases in the FY 2025 MedPAR file. Organ acquisition costs (kidney, heart, heart-lung, liver, lung, pancreas, intestinal) and hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges are subtracted from total charges on each transplant bill that showed such acquisition charges before computing average cost and eliminating outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains legal/ policy basis (organ acquisition paid on reasonable cost basis; Section 108 of Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020 for stem cell acquisition) and the necessity of subtracting these separately paid acquisition charges to avoid inflating average MS-DRG costs.
